title: Task Registry — source of truth for multi-agent orchestration
description: The orchestrator and every worker read/write this file (or an equivalent like GitHub Projects). Do NOT keep state in an agent's context.

agents.description: Worker pool. The orchestrator matches tasks by capabilities and picks by status=idle.

capabilities.description: Capability tags for matching. e.g. backend, frontend, sql, refactor, test, infra

max_concurrent.description: 1 worker = 1 task at a time is the safest

id.description: e.g. T-101; used as the branch slug feature/T-101

scope.description: File boundary — stops two workers from clobbering each other. Must be declared.

allow.description: globs of dirs/files the worker MAY change, e.g. src/payment/**

deny.description: globs that are strictly forbidden, e.g. src/shared/**

requires.description: Capabilities needed for the task — the orchestrator matches these against agents[].capabilities

depends_on.description: Tasks that must finish first (by id). The orchestrator won't assign until dependencies are merged.

state.description: Task lifecycle. The orchestrator drives the state transitions.

assignee.description: id of the agent holding the task

log.description: Decision/state-transition log for the task — RECONSTRUCTABLE context, NOT held in an agent's head. The orchestrator appends a line on each state change; record cross-cutting decisions in docs/decisions/ instead of here.

by.description: who wrote it: 'orchestrator' or an agent id

note.description: one line: what happened / what was decided
